limitations: Synthetic warm-cache native Result workloads; prepare/loading/hash validation excluded.
Variants and worker order reverse between rounds; query order is fixed.
Pure Go, GOAMD64=v1, normal build; 1 GiB query budget; ten-second per-query deadline.
This suite does not activate disk spilling or experimental hash controls.
The new round remains uncommitted; checkpoint48c9640 and the baseline runner match the first-round production state.
Native amd64 only. ARM64 normal/SIMD compilation uses vet disabled for existing assembly debt; no ARM runtime/throughput claim.
Fingerprint cache remains disabled in production; explicit experiment masks have scalar, AVX2 and NEON implementations.
Spill benchmarks select external execution explicitly; no adaptive transition, no streaming join-sort/limit/multijoin spilling.
Allocator budgets cover requested live segment bytes, excluding borrowed source, Go control metadata and idle slab capacity; they are not RSS limits.
Linux VmRSS is approximate and sampled peaks can miss transients; precise RSS/PSS endpoints and lifetime VmHWM are reported separately.
DuckDB Python fetchall conversion is timed, DataFusion native Arrow collect excludes Python conversion, and Polars shares columns; large-output comparisons are not pure-engine rankings.
Four-engine one-sample smoke timings are validation only; DataFusion54.0.0 CSV null-marker handling is unsupported.
Warm-cache synthetic fixtures with dyadic numeric values; no official TPC/ClickBench score.
Parallel multi-DISTINCT increases cold sampled RSS growth from148.0 to311.8 MiB (2.11x) at4workers on the million-row fixture; original source states coexist with merged sets.

limits: Per-operation cumulative Go allocations are not query-scope live-byte peaks.
Lookup tables are experimental controls explicitly enabled; production activation remains disabled.
Six executions per execution shape, two batches of100 complete selected scans, three100ms lookup samples.
Temporary-file throughput depends on this machine and filesystem; no native ARM measurements.
